subsystems.name: Entangled-pair source
subsystems.role: creates the photon pairs whose quantum correlations are the sensing resource.

subsystems.name: Idler storage
subsystems.role: holds the twin photons intact for the signal's round-trip time.
parts: quantum memory (atomic vapour or rare-earth crystal) or low-loss delay fibre

subsystems.name: Signal transmitter
subsystems.role: sends the probe photons towards the target.

subsystems.name: Receiver and joint measurement
subsystems.role: collects the faint return and measures it together with the idler rather than on its own.
parts: optical joint-detection receiver (e.g. a sum-frequency generation stage)

subsystems.name: Correlation processor
subsystems.role: turns photon time-stamps into a target-present or target-absent decision.

buildSteps.title: Generate the entanglement
buildSteps.detail: A laser pumps a nonlinear crystal; spontaneous parametric down-conversion emits photon pairs that are entangled in photon number and phase.

buildSteps.title: Choose and verify the wavelengths
buildSteps.detail: Signal and idler are split so the signal sits at a wavelength the atmosphere or target reflects well, then the correlations are measured to confirm the source is behaving.

buildSteps.title: Store the idler
buildSteps.detail: The idler is routed into a quantum memory or low-loss delay line long enough to survive the signal's journey to the target and back.

buildSteps.title: Illuminate the target
buildSteps.detail: The signal beam is aimed through a telescope; almost all photons are lost, and the few that return arrive buried in thermal background from the sun, sky and warm surroundings.

buildSteps.title: Collect the return
buildSteps.detail: A receiving telescope with narrow spectral, spatial and timing filters picks out the small band where signal photons can be found.

buildSteps.title: Measure jointly
buildSteps.detail: Return photons are measured together with their stored idlers — a joint-detection receiver, for example sum-frequency generation followed by photon counting, extracts correlations that no single-arm measurement can reveal.

buildSteps.title: Decide
buildSteps.detail: The process is repeated over many pulses; coincidence statistics are tested against a threshold, and because the noise acts differently on the two arms the correlation stands out even when the return alone looks like pure noise.

buildSteps.title: Engineer for the field
buildSteps.detail: Lasers, detectors, memory and timing are ruggedised and synchronised, then married to scanning optics. A radar version repeats all of this at microwave frequencies, where entanglement generation and memory are much harder.

prerequisites.why: the whole protocol rests on a bright, well-characterised source of correlated pairs.
the return is often a handful of photons, so detector dark counts set the floor.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum memories or low-loss delays at the operating wavelength
prerequisites.why: the idler must survive microseconds to milliseconds without losing its correlation.
demonstrated in laboratories, but needed in a compact, efficient form before field use.

prerequisites.tech: Microwave entanglement and microwave quantum memories
prerequisites.why: radar wavelengths are centimetres, where generating and storing entanglement is far harder than in optics.

pathway.milestone: laboratory demonstrations at optical wavelengths over short free-space paths, alongside theory showing an error-exponent advantage of up to roughly a factor of four at fixed transmitted energy
pathway.unlocks: proof that correlations survive loss and noise, and a clear statement of the regime where they help.

pathway.milestone: free-space trials at longer range against real daylight backgrounds, with idler storage that lasts long enough
pathway.unlocks: realistic loss budgets and a first honest comparison against classical illumination at equal energy.

pathway.milestone: compact, chip-scale joint-detection receivers and, separately, microwave entanglement sources
pathway.unlocks: a path from optical detection towards an actual quantum radar.

pathway.milestone: niche use where transmitted power must stay very low and the target reflects poorly
pathway.unlocks: low-signature sensing — but only if the advantage is shown to persist outside the few-photon regime, since classical illumination with more pulses or higher power is predicted to match it.
